audience.programmeDescription: The English-taught International Bachelor Economics and Business Economics at Erasmus School of Economics combines economic theory, business economics and quantitative methods. Students complete a major, a seminar and an individual thesis. This comparison shows one permitted 2026–2027 pathway with the Economics of Markets and Organisations major and a 12-EC minor.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR option combines economics and public policy with business strategy, accounting, financial decisions, marketing and data. The second adds psychology, health-related behaviour and evidence synthesis. The third gives more space to mathematical and computational analysis alongside accounting, securities, banking and economic decisions. These are related programmes with different priorities; they do not reproduce every specialist major, the seminar or the required thesis. Shared rows show partial curricular relationships.

curriculum.routeLabel: Economics of Markets and Organisations major; 12-EC minor
curriculum.limitation: One permitted 2026–2027 pathway is shown. The minor and School electives remain open within approval rules; other majors and the 15-EC minor/9-EC elective combination are available.

componentNotes.y3-major-seminar: Compulsory major seminar; entry requires completed Bachelor-1 and Bachelor-2. Seminar attendance is 100%.

componentNotes.y3-major-course3: Compulsory course in the selected major.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: Individual thesis on a subject from the selected major. Entry follows admission to the major seminar; IBEB does not require the seminar to have been passed first. Normal completion deadline is 1 October of the following academic year, subject to approved exceptions.
componentNotes.y1-math: The first year contains 60 EC plus compulsory zero-credit Guidance and Take-Off. Binding study advice normally requires all first-year units, with the published compensation and personal-circumstances provisions. Most first-year tutorials require 70% attendance; Guidance, Take-Off and major seminars require 100%. Later-year entry requires positive binding study advice.
